answer: Each identity surveys one atlas cell and locks a 70-credit bond, paying 29 credits; the k-th cell claimed from one source costs 29+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6023 and 1000 fake cells cost 3,026,000 plus 70,000 locked. A velvet ribbon marks the corners, and an auditor resurveys the cell against the atlas: a missing ribbon, a reused key, or one surveyor claiming two cells burns the bond. A rented-surveyor ring fails because its fable of two surveys collapses when the resurvey finds copied corners. An honest agent surveys one cell, pays 29 once, and reclaims the bond after a clean survey.
